create.name: Roshi Joan Halifax
create.bio:
Roshi Joan Halifax is a Zen teacher who founded Upaya Zen Center, a residential Zen community in Santa Fe, and still serves as its abbot. She started out as a cultural anthropologist and activist in the 1960s, came to Buddhism partly through Thich Nhat Hanh, began formal Zen practice in the 1970s with Seung Sahn, and later trained for nearly thirty years with Roshi Bernie Glassman. She has also studied with Tibetan teachers, among them Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche and the Dalai Lama. For decades she has worked with people who are dying and with those who care for them, and this sits at the centre of her teaching on compassion.

At Upaya she leads sesshins, practice periods and online programmes that join Zen meditation with socially engaged Buddhism, and she founded the Prajna Mountain Buddhist Order. She speaks to Buddhists and non-Buddhists alike about compassion, suffering and what it means to be human, and her own practice includes photography, brush painting and haiku. Her books include The Fruitful Darkness, Being with Dying and Standing at the Edge, which looks at how qualities such as empathy and engagement can turn harmful and how to find balance; she has also written Sophie Learns to Be Brave for children.

books.title: Standing at the Edge: Finding Freedom Where Fear and Courage Meet
books.author: Joan Halifax
books.description: A book on five qualities that help us serve others, among them altruism, empathy and engagement, and on how each can tip into harm. Drawing on her years of Zen practice and care work, she shows ways back to steadiness and compassion.

books.title: Being with Dying: Cultivating Compassion and Wisdom in the Presence of Death
books.author: Joan Halifax
books.description: Teachings and stories from her long work with dying people and their carers, with contemplative practices for meeting death, one's own or another's, with presence.

books.title: The Fruitful Darkness: A Journey Through Buddhist Practice
books.author: Joan Halifax
books.description: An account of her journeys through Buddhist practice, indigenous traditions and the natural world, exploring what she learnt from each about the shadow side of life.

books.title: Shaman: The Wounded Healer
books.author: Joan Halifax
books.description: An illustrated study of shamanic traditions around the world, from her work as an anthropologist.

books.title: Sophie Learns to Be Brave
books.author: Joan Halifax
books.description: A picture book for children aged four to eight in which a girl and a lost old dog face a thunderstorm together, with a simple breathing verse to steady them.

courses.title: ROHATSU: Circle of the Way (Online 2026)
courses.description: Upaya's annual week-long silent sesshin marking the Buddha's awakening, joined online. Days include sitting and walking meditation, formal meals, daily talks and practice interviews, with Roshi Joan and Sensei Kazuaki Tanahashi among the teachers.

courses.title: THE PATH of LOVE (Online February, 2027)
courses.description: A weekend programme with Roshi Joan Halifax and Henry Shukman, offered online by donation, with recordings for those registered.

courses.title: LOVE and DEATH: Opening the Great Gifts (Online 2027)
courses.description: A weekend with Frank Ostaseski and Roshi Joan on love and death as twin teachers, through talks, exchanges and practices around impermanence, service and surrender.
